description: Reference vectors for the crypto-transform oracle (SHA-256/SHA-1/MD5 + base64/hex), used by the applied-crypto MAP 'Sorting the Scramble' sort, the api-paradigms WS-Security digest recompute, and identity HS256 verification. The transform RECOMPUTES from learner bytes at runtime — these vectors only pin the engine's fidelity (it must reproduce them exactly). No learner string is ever stored.

provenance.computed_with: shasum -a 256/-a 1, md5, base64, xxd -p (macOS) and cross-checked vs node:crypto and python hashlib
provenance.honesty_note: Every value is a deterministic transform of its input, reproducible by anyone. SHA-256(empty)=e3b0c442... is the canonical empty-string digest cited across the curriculum. The api-paradigms WS-Security OASIS digest value is authored-with-citation (the OASIS normative example password is not published in full); the engine's job is to recompute Base64(SHA-1(nonce+created+password)) faithfully, which it does.

sort_classes.description: The 'Sorting the Scramble' MAP key — the class is DERIVED by running the real transform, not authored. base64/hex reverse with NO key => ENCODE; SHA-256/SHA-1/MD5 never reverse => HASH; AES reverses only WITH a key => ENCRYPT. The JWT-header card decodes with no key => ENCODE (the encoding-!=-protection lesson).
